To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found indications that the image quality and bio- feedback in a Virtual Reality intervention can affect anxiety levels, and that there are individual differences in how users manage attention.

1) the image quality of a VR system affects how well a user is able to perform a breathing task; 2) the image quality affects the user's anxiety levels, but not their self-reported stress; and 3) the image quality has a significant effect on the amount of time users spend in the breathing task.
